title: Joe's family, the band at his house, and Warren as inspiration
summary: His parents played guitar and piano; bands gathered at his house until train time, and watching Warren and Edgar made him want to play piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: My family, as my mother and father, were somewhat musically inclined. My father played guitar some years ago, and also the bass pedal. My mother used to play the piano. So much for that with Ogiee Socia, which I will just mention it, which my father played with, whose name is the same as mine. I'm a junior, otherwise I didn't mention that. In those days, I used to play with bass who sang quite often. And after the dance, it seems like my house has been, or our house, it wasn't mine at that time, it was there, would be the, where the band would congregate after knocking off. So, they would set up the instruments, they had no such lawyers to, what time you should play, we could play up to sunrise. So they'd play a night if you wanted. Right. So the band would set up and they'd play there until, let's say, number two. That's the train they would go back on. They had no highways at that time. So they still didn't play until the time for the train, well we didn't live too far from the station. What time, number two, or what? Around, say, 5, 540, somewhere in the neighborhood.
In other words, when they knock off of the job, they come into your house and play until train time.

Until train time, that's correct. Now, as the year went by, Ogeet's son Edgar, played the saxophone, and Warren played clarinet and piano. And that's where the first idea of me wanting to play the piano is watching Warren and Edgar.

Yeah, that is correct. So, as a kid I'd be up and I'd be watching and listening. I guess I just loved music. So, as time went on, Warren would come back over, as teenagers would do in those days.
